findings.proof: For normalized Maxwellian f0, fε=f0+ε onB1/ε. Mass>=4π/3 ε^-2 and energy>=4π/5 ε^-4. Mass conservation implies ||sqrtfε(t)-sqrtf0||2>=sqrt(mε)-1→∞ at all times; weightedL∞k difference atv=(1/(2ε),0,0)>=2^-k ε^(1-k). The6Dtail lackswdecay; correcting it alone leaves ε^-5massplateau.
findings.counterevidence: Formal lifted/sphere dissipation remains consistent. Gaussian stationary datum is not a main-theorem counterexample. Gaussian additive initial perturbation can repair initial norms, but full PDE/Fisher stability remains to be supplied.

focused_acceptance.reason: The actual constant floor on B(1/epsilon) forces mass>=4pi/(3epsilon2) and energy>=4pi/(5epsilon4) for an admissible unit Maxwellian. Mass conservation precludes claimed square-root H1 convergence at every common time; the6D formula additionally lacks w-decay. AppendixB explicitly justifies the extension of Theorem1.1. Retain Major for this proof passage, not a blow-up or false-main-theorem claim. Gaussian perturbation repairs initial norms only; full PDE/Fisher stability is not asserted.
